Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

don't and doesn't — the Present Simple negative.
In other words
“I don't have a lot of free time.”
“He doesn't wear special clothes for work.”
“We don't get up early at weekends.”
“They don't usually go out on Fridays.”
Notice

Notice: after he — don't or doesn't? And what happens to the main verb?

PersonNegativeExample
I / you / we / theydon't + base verbI don't have a lot of free time.
he / she / itdoesn't + base verbHe doesn't wear special clothes.
careful!no -s after doesn'tShe doesn't works ✗ → She doesn't work ✓
In other words
don't = do not · doesn't = does not.
I / you / we / they → don't. He / she / it → doesn't.
After doesn't the -s disappears — the “s” lives in does: he doesn't work.
Frequency adverbs go after don't/doesn't: “He doesn't always have breakfast.”
Questions with Do you…? / Does he…? come in Lesson 9.

Stage 7 · Listen

Listen

Track 2.7 — the astronaut's dayOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
All astronauts in Europe learn their job at the European Astronaut Centre in Cologne in Germany. The training is hard, but it's interesting and I love it. My day starts at ten to seven when I get up. I have a shower and then have breakfast in the canteen at quarter to eight. Classes begin at half past eight. In the morning, we study things like engineering and physics. At quarter past eleven, we stop and have a break. I usually have a coffee and I also try and learn some Russian vocabulary. We all learn Russian here. Classes start again at half past eleven. Lunch is at one o'clock, and in the afternoons we have more classes from quarter past two. We learn to use the space equipment and machines and we also have language classes. Classes finish at quarter to six. I always feel really tired, but I often go to the gym in the evening. I'm in bed by ten o'clock and by five past ten I'm usually asleep.
Track 2.11 — astronaut factsOriginal coursebook recording

1 Most astronauts don't feel well when they first go into space. Space sickness is very common. 2 Astronauts don't wear special clothes in the space station. They only need a space suit when they go on a spacewalk. 3 Astronauts don't change their clothes every day. It isn't possible to wash clothes in space. 4 Astronauts usually exercise for two hours a day. 5 Usually, an astronaut doesn't go on a spacewalk more than once a week. 6 Most astronauts sleep for less time in space but they don't feel very tired.
1Astronauts wear special clothes inside the space station.
2They change their clothes every day.
3They usually exercise for two hours a day.
Why

They don't wear special clothes inside and don't change clothes every day — but they DO exercise two hours a day.

Stage 8 · Write

Write

Track 2.17 — are you free after class?Original coursebook recording
Show transcript
A: Are you free after class today? B: I'm sorry, but I'm busy this evening. But I don't have any plans tomorrow. A: Would you like to go out for a pizza? B: Yes, I'd love to. What time shall we meet? A: Eight o'clock at Gino's? Or do you want to meet at the station? B: Yes, let's meet there at 7.45. A: OK, see you then!
Useful language
  • Are you free…?
  • I'm sorry, but I'm busy.
  • I don't have any plans.
  • I'd love to!
  • What time shall we meet?
  • Let's meet at…
Two friends agree when to meet. Listen.

Then write your own mini dialogue.

1When is B free?
2Where do they meet in the end?
Why

B is busy this evening but free tomorrow. They meet at the station at quarter to eight.

Invite your partner — and agree a time to meet.

Listen to the model first.

Invite your teacher — and agree a time to meet.

Listen to the model first.

In other words
Step 1 — invite your partner (pizza, cinema, a walk). They are busy the first time — they say no politely and give a reason.
Step 2 — find a time you are both free. Agree a place and an exact time (quarter past seven, half past six…).
Step 3 — swap roles and repeat with a new invitation.
In other words

Step 3 — swap roles and repeat with a new invitation.
Stage 9 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1She ___ eat meat. (negative)
2I ___ like Mondays. (negative)
3We meet ___ six o'clock.
Why

I/you/we/they \u2192 don't \u00b7 he/she/it \u2192 doesn't \u00b7 times take AT: at six o'clock.

1She don't eat meat.
2I doesn't like Mondays.
3We meet in six o'clock.
Why

I/you/we/they \u2192 don't \u00b7 he/she/it \u2192 doesn't \u00b7 times take AT: at six o'clock.

1Make it negative: I drink coffee.
2Make it negative: She likes tea.
3Write 7:30 in words.
Why

I/you/we/they \u2192 don't \u00b7 he/she/it \u2192 doesn't \u00b7 times take AT: at six o'clock.
